A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HERMES and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H. Matching content across table renumbering and page shifts supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, HERMES benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds Qwen3-VL evaluations and experiments on layer-budget allocation and guidance prompts.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B, C, E, and F retain HERMES's importance scoring, cross-layer smoothing, position re-indexing, guidance strategy, and summary-token aggregation. The additional backbones and ablation configurations do not establish a revision to the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate StreamingBench, the same OVO-Bench subsets, RVS-Ego/RVS-Movie, MVBench, Egoschema, and VideoMME. The new backbone and sensitivity experiments remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3-VL-4B as base-model comparators alongside their HERMES variants. Existing comparator membership in the other benchmark and efficiency comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds 4B/8B Qwen3-VL evaluations at 2 fps and new controlled configuration sweeps. The layer-budget experiment fixes total memory at 6000 times the layer count while varying allocation weights; the prompt experiment tests three alternatives. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and default evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds systematic tests of two previously untested design choices: layer-dependent memory allocation at fixed total capacity (Table 5), and guidance-prompt sensitivity on two backbones (Table 10). Both span StreamingBench, OVO-Bench, and VideoMME, substantially extending the analysis beyond the retained budget-size, smoothing, re-indexing, and aggregation ablations.

E5.justification: There is no added or revised seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence interval, or significance test. The new tables continue reporting point estimates, and the original attention-averaging protocol is retained.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover Qwen3-VL and the two sensitivity studies. For example, Table 1 newly reports 81.28% StreamingBench accuracy and 61.29% OVO-Bench average for Qwen3-VL-8B with HERMES at 4K tokens and 2 fps. Most existing results are retained, but Table 3 changes TPOT at chunk size 16 and 512 frames from 53.63 to 23.63 ms under the same stated settings.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 newly defines proportional per-layer budget allocation using normalized weights, integer flooring, and residual assignment to preserve total capacity. This is a limited mathematical definition for the new ablation; the existing scoring and RoPE mathematics remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical KV memory, training-free streaming inference, up to 68% token reduction, 11.4% accuracy gains, and 10-fold latency speedup. The added experiments support existing claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablations as showing limited sensitivity to allocation weights and guidance prompts, and connects larger deep-layer budgets with long-term memory preservation. Its new Limitations paragraph explicitly identifies untested 72B models and combinations with other training-free techniques.

D1.justification: v3 documents the allocation weights, normalization and rounding procedure, and literal alternative prompts. Table 1 supplies sampling rates for the added Qwen3 models and replaces Flash-VStream's unspecified rate with 1 fps. Existing hardware, precision, default prompts, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion are unchanged. Qwen3-VL was already cited as reference 4 in v1; its added evaluation does not introduce a new cited work or revise the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The edits are localized: Section 4.4 gains two analysis passages, Memory Budget becomes Total Memory Budget, and Limitations and Acknowledgment sections are added. Author affiliation and correspondence details also change. Most prose and the principal section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds two ablation tables, expands Table 1, moves main-text table captions above their tables, and regroups existing ablation tables. Figures retain their content and design; appendix tables are renumbered without substantive display changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Tables 5 and 10 provide useful evidence about previously untested allocation and prompt choices, while Table 1 broadens support for applicability to another model family. The new limitations also clarify validation boundaries. These gains are incremental, and integration remains incomplete: Section 4.1 still describes only the original two model families despite the Qwen3 results.
